concepts.title: Game Loop และ Delta Time (จำลองด้วย Python)
concepts.covers: Teaches: what a game loop is (process input -> update -> render, repeated every frame); frame, FPS and frame time (60 FPS = 16.67 ms per frame); delta time and why every movement and timer must be multiplied by delta; variable timestep (Godot _process) vs fixed timestep (Godot _physics_process, 60 ticks per second by default); the accumulator pattern; clamping a huge delta after a freeze (the 'spiral of death'). Part 1 Step 2 already shows delta_demo.py (30/60/144 FPS, 4 px per frame vs 200 px/s * delta), so do NOT repeat that example. Code: /home/somchai/projects/gamedev-lab/c01_game_loop.py, standard library only and fully deterministic (no time.sleep, no real clock): feed a fixed list of simulated frame times in seconds, e.g. [0.016, 0.016, 0.033, 0.050, 0.008, 0.400], into a loop that (1) clamps each frame time to MAX_DELTA = 0.1, (2) adds it to an accumulator and runs as many fixed physics steps of 1/60 s as fit, moving x by SPEED = 200 px/s * fixed step, (3) prints one line per frame: frame number, frame time in ms, physics steps run this frame, x position (f-strings, fixed decimals). End with a summary line (total simulated time, steps, final x). Run with python3 c01_game_loop.py in WSL and paste the real output. Mistakes table: real Python errors (ZeroDivisionError when computing FPS from a 0.0 frame time; TypeError when concatenating str and float) plus the logic bug of forgetting delta.

concepts.title: Node, Scene, Scene Tree และ Instancing
concepts.covers: Teaches: Node as the building block (Node, Node2D, Sprite2D, CollisionShape2D, Area2D, CharacterBody2D, Control) and the Inspector; a Scene is a saved tree of nodes (.tscn) that can be instanced many times; root, parent, child, sibling; Scene dock vs FileSystem dock; get_node() / $Child / %UniqueName, get_parent(), get_children(), add_child(), remove_child(), queue_free(); preload() vs load(); PackedScene.instantiate(); print_tree_pretty(). Example in the godot-lab project: res://c02_scene_tree/coin.tscn (Area2D 'Coin' with a Sprite2D using res://icon.svg at scale 0.25 and a CollisionShape2D with CircleShape2D radius 16, built in the editor: list the clicks) and res://c02_scene_tree/world.tscn (Node2D 'World') with world.gd: preload coin.tscn, instantiate 3 coins named Coin1..Coin3 at x = 100, 200, 300 (set position BEFORE add_child), call print_tree_pretty(), print get_child_count(), then queue_free() Coin2, await get_tree().process_frame and print the count again. Run with F6. print_tree_pretty() draws the tree with box-drawing characters: run it headless with the sandbox binary and copy the real output exactly. Mistakes: wrong node path (Node not found error), calling instantiate() on a null PackedScene, adding the same node twice with add_child(): get the exact error texts by running them headless.

concepts.title: GDScript พื้นฐานแบบมี Static Typing
concepts.covers: Teaches GDScript to someone who already knows Python (topic 9): extends, var/const, static typing (var hp: int = 3, inferred :=, return types -> int / -> void), built-in types int, float, bool, String, Vector2, Array and typed Array[int], Dictionary, enum, if/elif/else, match, for over range()/arrays/dictionaries, while, functions with default arguments, string formatting with % and str(), print(); differences from Python (func instead of def, true/false/null, no list comprehensions, and/or/not, tabs are the editor default). Example: res://c03_gdscript/basics.gd (Part 1 Step 4 already used res://c03_gdscript/hello.gd, so use this new file) extends Node; in _ready(): enum Difficulty {EASY, NORMAL, HARD}, a typed Array[Dictionary] of 3 enemy definitions (name, hp, speed), func spawn_interval(difficulty: Difficulty) -> float using match (EASY 1.5, NORMAL 1.2, HARD 0.8), loops that print a formatted table and the total HP, and a typed helper returning int. Attach to a Node in basics.tscn and press F6. Verify the output headless. Mistakes: assigning a String to an int variable (static type error), mixing tabs and spaces (verified in 4.7.2: 'Parse Error: Used space character for indentation instead of tab as used before in the file.'), calling a function with the wrong number of arguments (get the exact text headless).

concepts.title: Lifecycle Callback, @export และ @onready
concepts.covers: Teaches the order Godot calls node functions: _init(), _enter_tree() (parent before children), _ready() (children before parent), then every frame _process(delta) and at a fixed 60 ticks per second _physics_process(delta); _unhandled_input(event) for one-shot input events; set_process(false); @export (and @export_range(0, 1000, 10)) to edit values in the Inspector; @onready var label: Label = $Label to grab child nodes once they exist, and why a class-level var using $Child without @onready is null. Example: res://c04_lifecycle/lifecycle.tscn with parent.gd on Node2D 'Parent' and child.gd on its child Node2D 'Child', both printing their _enter_tree/_ready messages so the order is visible; parent.gd also counts _physics_process calls, and after exactly 60 physics frames prints the count and the fixed delta (Godot 4.7.2 prints the physics delta as 0.01666666666667), then calls get_tree().quit(); include @export var speed: float = 200.0 shown in the Inspector. Count frames, never wall-clock time, so the output is the same on every machine. Verify with: <godot> --headless --path <lab> --fixed-fps 60 res://c04_lifecycle/lifecycle.tscn.

concepts.title: Input Map, Vector2 และการเคลื่อนที่ด้วย CharacterBody2D
concepts.covers: Teaches: creating actions in Project > Project Settings > Input Map (move_left = A/Left, move_right = D/Right, move_up = W/Up, move_down = S/Down, pause = Esc/P, plus gamepad left stick and D-pad); Input.get_vector("move_left", "move_right", "move_up", "move_down") (length capped at 1 so diagonals are not faster), Input.is_action_just_pressed("pause"); Vector2 math: length(), normalized(), distance_to(), direction_to(), angle(), rad_to_deg(), lerp(), move_toward(); the diagonal speed bug (Vector2(1, 1).length() is about 1.414); CharacterBody2D with the velocity property and move_and_slide() (Godot 4: no arguments), acceleration and friction with velocity.move_toward(target, accel * delta), clamping position to the 1152 x 648 viewport. Example: res://c05_movement/player.gd (extends CharacterBody2D, @export speed 300.0, accel 1500.0, friction 1200.0) plus res://c05_movement/vector_demo.gd that prints the vector math results. For a deterministic movement output, a test scene can call Input.action_press("move_right") and print the position after 60 physics frames: verified in 4.7.2 with --fixed-fps 60 that 60 frames at 300 px/s give x = 300.000030517578 (float32 rounding), so print with "%.1f" or snappedf() and explain the tiny error. Mistakes: misspelled action (verified format: The InputMap action "move_lefft" doesn't exist. Did you mean "move_left"?), Godot 3 code move_and_slide(velocity) or KinematicBody2D (get exact errors headless).

concepts.title: Physics และ Collision: Area2D, Layer/Mask, Signal และ Group
concepts.covers: Teaches: body types StaticBody2D / CharacterBody2D / RigidBody2D / Area2D and when to use each; CollisionShape2D; collision_layer (what I am) vs collision_mask (what I look for) with named layers in Project Settings > Layer Names > 2D Physics: 1 player, 2 enemies, 3 stars, 4 walls; Area2D signals body_entered / area_entered; connecting signals in the Node dock vs in code (body_entered.connect(_on_body_entered)); custom signals with typed arguments; groups (add_to_group("player"), is_in_group(), get_tree().get_nodes_in_group()); never change physics state directly inside a physics callback: use set_deferred("monitoring", false) or call_deferred(); queue_free(). Example consistent with Part 1 Step 6: res://c06_collision/star.gd (extends Area2D, signal collected(points: int), checks body.is_in_group("player"), emits collected.emit(10), then queue_free()), a player in group "player", and game.gd that connects to collected and prints the running score, e.g. "เก็บดาว +10 คะแนนรวม 10". For a headless check, place the player overlapping the star (or move it for a few physics frames) and print. Mistakes: mask not set so nothing is detected (no error at all: debug with Debug > Visible Collision Shapes), missing CollisionShape2D (editor warning), connecting the same signal twice (get the exact error text headless).

concepts.title: Sprite, Animation และ TileMapLayer
concepts.covers: Teaches: Sprite2D (texture, flip_h, modulate, scale); pixel-art import (Project Settings > Rendering > Textures > Canvas Textures > Default Texture Filter = Nearest); AnimatedSprite2D with SpriteFrames (play("run"), stop(), animation_finished, sprite sheets from Kenney CC0 packs); AnimationPlayer (tracks for any property, keyframes, call-method tracks, play/queue) and when to choose which; TileMapLayer (TileMap is deprecated since 4.3): TileSet resource, atlas source, painting tiles, a physics layer on the TileSet for walls, two TileMapLayer nodes (Ground, Walls), and the code API set_cell(coords: Vector2i, source_id, atlas_coords), erase_cell(), get_used_cells(), local_to_map() / map_to_local(). Example: res://c07_animation/player_anim.gd choosing "idle"/"run" and flip_h from velocity, and res://c07_animation/arena.gd that builds a rectangular wall border on a TileMapLayer with set_cell() in loops (e.g. 20 x 12 tiles, so get_used_cells().size() = 2*20 + 2*10 = 60) and prints local_to_map() for a sample position with 64 px tiles. Create the TileSet in code (TileSet.new(), TileSetAtlasSource using res://icon.svg, texture_region_size 64 x 64, create_tile()) so the example also runs headless; verify every number headless.

concepts.title: Camera2D, UI และเสียง
concepts.covers: Teaches: Camera2D (enabled, zoom, position_smoothing_enabled and speed, limit_left/top/right/bottom, offset used later for shake); world space vs screen space; CanvasLayer so the HUD does not move with the camera; Control nodes Label, Button, TextureRect, ProgressBar; VBoxContainer / HBoxContainer / MarginContainer / CenterContainer and anchor presets; Theme resource and theme overrides; Button.pressed signal; keyboard/gamepad focus with grab_focus(); a pause menu with get_tree().paused = true and process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS on the menu; audio: AudioStreamPlayer vs AudioStreamPlayer2D, .wav for short SFX and .ogg (loop enabled in the Import dock) for music, buses Master / Music / SFX in the Audio dock, AudioServer.get_bus_index(), set_bus_volume_db(idx, linear_to_db(v)), random pitch_scale 0.9-1.1. Example: res://c08_camera_ui_audio/hud.gd (CanvasLayer with ScoreLabel and LivesLabel updated through signals; prints the label text after each update) and audio_settings.gd consistent with Part 1 Step 8 (func set_bus_volume(bus_name: String, linear: float) -> void) that prints the dB values for 1.0, 0.5, 0.25 and 0.0 (0.5 is about -6.02 dB; 0.0 gives -inf): verify the exact printed values headless (create the Music/SFX buses with AudioServer.add_bus() for the headless test, and explain the Audio dock for the editor). Mistakes: HUD placed in world space and scrolling away, pause menu frozen because process_mode was not ALWAYS, get_bus_index() with a misspelled bus name returning -1.

concepts.title: Timer, Spawning และอายุของ Object
concepts.covers: Teaches: the Timer node (wait_time, one_shot, autostart, timeout signal, start()/stop()); await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout for one-off delays; preload() vs load(); PackedScene.instantiate() and setting position before add_child(); RandomNumberGenerator with a fixed seed for reproducible tests; the difficulty ramp exactly as Part 1 Step 9 (wait_time starts at 1.2 s, multiplied by 0.97 after each spawn, minimum 0.35 s; spawn at x = randf_range(0, 1152), y = -40); removing objects with queue_free(), VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D.screen_exited or a y > 700 check; measuring leaks with Performance.get_monitor(Performance.OBJECT_NODE_COUNT) and Debugger > Monitors; object pooling only after measuring a real problem. Example: res://c09_spawning/spawner.gd plus enemy.tscn (Area2D moving down at 200 px/s, freed below y = 700) printing the spawn interval for the first 10 spawns (deterministic: 1.2, 1.164, 1.12908 ...) and the node count once per simulated second to show it stays stable. Verify headless with --fixed-fps 60 and count physics frames instead of wall-clock time.

concepts.title: Autoload, การสลับ Scene และการบันทึกข้อมูล
concepts.covers: Teaches: Autoload singletons (Project Settings > Globals > Autoload) and the GameState pattern from Part 1 Step 10 (score, lives = 3, high_score; signals score_changed(new_score: int) and lives_changed(new_lives: int); reset(), add_score(points: int), lose_life()), pros and cons of global state; get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://...") and change_scene_to_packed(); res:// is read-only after export while user:// is writable (Windows: %APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\<project name>\); ConfigFile for settings and high score (user://savegame.cfg with [progress] high_score and [settings] screen_shake, music_volume, sfx_volume); FileAccess with JSON.stringify() / JSON.parse_string() for a top-5 score list in user://scores.json (note that JSON numbers come back as float: verify and show it); FileAccess.file_exists(), error_string(err), defensive loading (missing file, wrong types); security rule: never load .tres/.res files supplied by users because resources can embed scripts. Example: res://c10_state_save/save_manager.gd with save_high_score() / load_high_score() (same code as Part 1 Step 10: SAVE_PATH = "user://savegame.cfg", section "progress", key "high_score") plus save_top_scores(scores: Array[int]) / load_top_scores() using JSON, printing a full round trip. The page shows the Windows path for somchai, e.g. C:/Users/somchai/AppData/Roaming/Godot/app_userdata/godot-lab/scores.json, with a note that it differs per machine; the logic itself is verified headless (the Linux path differs).

concepts.title: State Machine สำหรับผู้เล่นและ AI ของศัตรู
concepts.covers: Teaches: why many booleans (is_dashing, is_hurt, is_stunned) create impossible combinations; the finite state machine: states, transitions, enter/exit actions, exactly one current state; the enum + match FSM consistent with Part 1 Step 11 (enemy_chaser.gd with enum State {IDLE, CHASE, STUNNED}, detect_radius = 250, stop chasing beyond detect_radius * 1.5 to avoid flicker, change_state() printing "IDLE -> CHASE"); the node-based FSM (a StateMachine node with child State nodes exposing enter(), exit(), physics_update(delta)) for bigger characters; drawing a state diagram; keeping logic testable by separating it from nodes. Example: res://c11_state_machine/enemy_brain.gd (class_name EnemyBrain extends RefCounted) whose update(distance: float, delta: float) returns the current state, prints every transition, and supports a STUNNED state lasting 0.5 s via a countdown; plus test_brain.gd (extends SceneTree, run with --headless --script) that feeds a fixed list of distances and one stun event, printing each transition and a final line with the number of transitions. Paste the real headless output.

concepts.title: Tween, Game Feel และ Performance
concepts.covers: Teaches: Tween via create_tween() (tween_property, set_trans(Tween.TRANS_BACK / TRANS_ELASTIC / TRANS_SINE), set_ease, parallel(), chain(), tween_callback(), set_loops(), kill(), the finished signal; a tween belongs to the node that created it); game feel ("juice"): screen shake with trauma as in Part 1 Step 12 (shake_camera.gd: add_trauma(amount), trauma decreases by decay * delta with decay = 2.0, offset scaled by trauma squared, max_offset = 12 px), hit flash with modulate, squash and stretch, hitstop with Engine.time_scale = 0.05 and get_tree().create_timer(0.08, true, false, true) (4th argument ignore_time_scale), CPUParticles2D with one_shot (recommended with the Compatibility renderer), random pitch; an accessibility option to turn shake off (saved in [settings] screen_shake); measuring the cost of effects with Debugger > Monitors, Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_PROCESS) and the Profiler. Example: res://c12_game_feel/juice_demo.gd: a tween sequence on a Sprite2D whose finished callback prints the final scale and modulate, and a trauma printout for the first frames after add_trauma(0.6) at 60 FPS (deterministic: 0.6 -> 0.5667 -> 0.5333 ...). Verify headless with --fixed-fps 60. Export and Git are taught in the Part 4 Mini Project, not as a concept here.

mini_project.name: 2D Arcade Game: Star Dodger
mini_project.summary: เกม Arcade 2D มุมมองจากด้านบน (Top-down) ธีมอวกาศ ผู้เล่นบังคับยานเดิน 8 ทิศ หลบศัตรูที่เกิดจากขอบบนของจอถี่ขึ้นเรื่อยๆ และเก็บดาวเพื่อได้คะแนน เริ่มด้วย 3 ชีวิต ชนศัตรูเสีย 1 ชีวิตพร้อมช่วงอมตะ 1 วินาที หมดชีวิตแล้วไปหน้า Game Over ที่แสดงคะแนนและ High Score ซึ่งบันทึกลงดิสก์ มีเพลง เสียงเอฟเฟกต์ เมนู Pause, Game Feel (จอสั่น, Tween, Particle) และ Export เป็นไฟล์ Windows (.exe) พร้อมเวอร์ชัน Web สำหรับ itch.io. It is the same game designed in Part 1 (GDD gdd-star-dodger.md in Step 1, built up through Steps 5-13, released in Step 14). There is NO shooting: the core loop is dodge enemies -> collect stars -> score -> enemies spawn faster -> lose -> retry for a higher score.
features: Main Menu (scenes/main_menu.tscn, scripts/main_menu.gd): title, Play and Quit buttons, shows the saved High Score, Play button gets keyboard/gamepad focus with grab_focus().

Player (scenes/player.tscn, scripts/player.gd, class_name Player, in group "player"): CharacterBody2D, 8-direction movement with Input.get_vector("move_left", "move_right", "move_up", "move_down") at 300 px/s, position clamped to the 1152 x 648 viewport, 1.0 s invincibility with blinking after a hit.

Enemies (scenes/enemy.tscn, scripts/enemy.gd): Area2D that falls from y = -40 at a random x between 0 and 1152 with a random speed of 150-250 px/s and frees itself off-screen (VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D); spawned by SpawnTimer in scripts/game.gd: wait_time starts at 1.2 s, multiplied by 0.97 after each spawn, minimum 0.35 s (same as Part 1 Step 9). Optional extra: the chaser enemy from Part 1 Step 11 (scenes/enemy_chaser.tscn, enum State {IDLE, CHASE, STUNNED}).

Stars (scenes/star.tscn, scripts/star.gd): Area2D with signal collected(points: int), worth 10 points, spawned every 2.0 s at a random position inside the viewport; pop Tween, CPUParticles2D burst and pickup sound when collected.
Collision layers named in Project Settings: 1 player, 2 enemies, 3 stars, 4 walls.

Game state Autoload GameState (scripts/game_state.gd): score, lives = 3, high_score; signals score_changed(new_score: int) and lives_changed(new_lives: int); functions reset(), add_score(points: int), lose_life().

High score saved to disk with Autoload SaveManager (scripts/save_manager.gd): ConfigFile at user://savegame.cfg, section "progress" key "high_score"; section "settings" keys "screen_shake" (bool), "music_volume" and "sfx_volume" (linear 0.0-1.0); missing or corrupt file falls back to defaults.
HUD (scenes/hud.tscn, scripts/hud.gd): CanvasLayer with labels Score, Lives and Best, updated only through GameState signals.
Pause menu: action pause (Esc and P) toggles get_tree().paused; the menu uses process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS and has Resume, Screen Shake On/Off and Main Menu buttons.
Audio: buses Master, Music, SFX; looping music .ogg on Music; sfx_pickup.wav, sfx_hit.wav and sfx_game_over.wav on SFX with random pitch_scale 0.9-1.1.
Game feel: scripts/shake_camera.gd (add_trauma(0.6) on hit, decay 2.0, max_offset 12.0), hit flash with modulate, star pop tween, short hitstop of 0.08 s.
Game Over (scenes/game_over.tscn, scripts/game_over.gd): final score, "New High Score!" when beaten, Retry and Main Menu buttons.

Export: preset "Windows Desktop" to build/windows/StarDodger.exe and preset "Web" to build/web/index.html (Compatibility renderer, Thread Support off); export from the editor and from PowerShell with --headless --export-release.

Verification step: tools/smoke_test.gd from Part 1 Step 14 (extends SceneTree, 16 checks: version, main scene, 5 input actions, 7 scenes, scripts parse, user:// round trip); run with --headless --path . --script res://tools/smoke_test.gd; expected last line 'สรุป: ผ่าน 16 ข้อ ไม่ผ่าน 0 ข้อ' and $LASTEXITCODE 0.

Export Templates 4.7.2.stable (must match the editor exactly). Python 3.12.3 (system python3 on Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL2) for c01 only, standard library only, no pip packages. Git 2.43.0 (apt). Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on WSL2 for Python, Git and command-line work; the Godot editor runs on Windows 10/11 directly (not inside WSL). C# is optional: Godot .NET edition needs the .NET SDK version stated in the Godot docs (do not guess a number). Unity: no version pinned, tell learners to check the latest LTS at unity.com.
